notes: Every rule is a multiple of the cable outer diameter (radius = multiple x OD); treat as minimums and use the governing (largest) applicable rule.
od_status 'catalogue' = value taken from a manufacturer catalogue or utility schedule, not a model; it has not been re-checked against a product drawing in this pass.
Source keys S1..S8 are listed in docs/cables-sources.md.

rules.source: Single-core unarmoured 11-33 kV (BS 7870-4.10 / 4.11): 20 x OD during installation, a manufacturer installation rule (S2)
Same class: 15 x OD in the final position, bent with a former at joints and terminations (BS 6622) (S2)
Single-core armoured 6.6-33 kV (BS 6622 / BS 7835): 15 x OD during installation (S2)
Same class: 12 x OD in the final position (S2)
Our generic rule for XLPE single-core 33 kV: 20 x OD during and after installation; consistent with a UK network operator policy (S3 Table 8, cited by number only)
US practice (AEIC/ICEA, NEC 300.34): training radius of three single 5-35 kV wire-shielded cables, 5 x the assembly diameter (about 2.155 x single-cable OD); final position only (S5)
XLPE single-core 66-132 kV with a solid metallic sheath, pulled into ducts: 35 x OD (S3 Table 8)
Same class, laid direct: 30 x OD (S3 Table 8)
Same class, next to joints and terminations: 20 x OD (S3 Table 8)
Manufacturer installation advice for 66 kV and above: of the order of 30 x OD minimum (S2)
Public utility tender specification (2019), 132 kV single core: 20 x OD during installation (S7)
An HV XLPE land cable user's guide, laminated or lead-sheathed design: 18 x OD at laying (S4)
Same guide: 12 x OD when installed (S4)
Same guide, standard design (copper wire screen only): 15 x OD at laying (S4)
Same guide: 10 x OD when installed (S4)
No open source found for a 132 kV trefoil-specific rule; the operator policy applies the multiple per single cable whatever the formation (S3, S8)
